analysis:
All three changed files are documentation only (docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md, docs/developer/build.md, docs/developer/test.md). They change no executable code, endpoints, or deployment settings.

prefix-cache.md: the patch excerpt is truncated, and units 6-7 show only head lines 442-862. Per the excerpt, the recurrent checkpoint bank table row (head ~295) now adds the "plain unpublished Nemotron Super owner" to the eligible families. The new text describes `alignsRecurrentCheckpointsToPrefillChunks`, which captures only at fixed prefill-chunk multiples reached by whole chunks. The code behind this is not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot confirm the new eligibility or capture rule; this is a coverage limit, not evidence of a defect. Relevant to T-041 (prefix cache TTFT oracle and at-rest artifacts) and TB-007: if Nemotron Super recurrent checkpoints were extended to SSD or complete-checkpoint stores, the scope, HMAC-tag, TTL and epoch properties from T-041 must still hold. This pass has nothing to confirm that they do. The visible lines 442-862 are unchanged context and still describe authenticated manifests, salt/scope binding, the bounded TTL and the corruption fallback. The "plain unpublished" wording suggests it is not published or enabled in production.

build.md (added at head 253-259) and test.md (head 487-505, patch only) add Nemotron qualification-harness documentation. They say fixture passes do not qualify the shipping provider, and they reference `NEMOTRON_SUPER_REFERENCE_DIR`, which is test-only. They make no production-activation claim and weaken no control.

For integration: if any batch contains Swift code for Nemotron Super recurrent checkpoint reuse, check cacheSalt scoping, identity binding and the KEK-derived HMAC lookup under T-041.
